incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44; ss. 5-10 (incorporation), 12 (share structure), 13 (registered office), 14 (directors), 17 (commencement of existence), 20 (corporate records), 104 (officers); Investment Canada Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. 28 (1st Supp.) for non-resident ownership.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED); Ontario Business Registry for extra-provincial registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) filed through Corporations Canada's online portal; Ontario Extra-Provincial Registration via Ontario Business Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the CBCA; the Corporation may establish any authorized share capital. No escrow account is required. Directors must issue shares for adequate consideration, and non-resident ownership is permitted subject to Investment Canada Act net benefit review above statutory thresholds.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: 1. The Corporation subscribes for the minimum issued shares as set forth in the Articles; the directors are authorized to allot and issue the subscription shares to the incorporator upon full payment of the agreed consideration. 2. The registered office shall be established at the Ontario address stated in the Articles and the named law agent/first director as custodian of corporate records. 3. The following individuals are appointed as first directors/officers: [Name], President; [Name], Secretary; [Name], Treasurer, each to serve until the first annual meeting. 4. Corporate seals, banking resolutions, good standing filings, and Ontario extra-provincial registration are authorized. 5. The directors are empowered to open bank accounts, designate signing officers, and engage professional advisors to obtain all operating and high-risk payment licenses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation Name Search and NUANS Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada; NUANS system via ISED or accredited search house.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS name search using the proposed corporate name. If the name is not confusingly similar to existing corporate names and shows no conflicting trademark, reserve the name. No notarization is required; the NUANS report is submitted with the Articles in Step 3.
required_dossiers: Director information and principal Ontario jurisdiction statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as confusingly similar, file an amended NUANS request with a revised distinctive element or request the written consent of the conflicting name holder.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada online portal; Ontario Business Registry later for extra-provincial registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare Form 1 Articles of Incorporation containing the corporate name, registered office address in Ontario, authorized share classes with rights and restrictions, number of directors, and any permitted restrictions on business activities. Articles may be signed in counterpart; each incorporator's signature must be witnessed. Notarization is not required, but if an external service provider files, attestation rules apply.
required_dossiers: Initial registered office address and mailing address in Ontario
Name and address of first directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing package is incomplete, Corporations Canada issues a deficiency notice; correct the omitted fields via the same portal within 30 days and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit Articles and Pay Government Filing Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada online filing system (Company and Bankruptcies Search System).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the Corporations Canada portal, upload the executed Form 1 and NUANS requirement, pay the CAD 200 processing fee by credit card, and verify the submission confirmation. No physical book is required at filing; original documents and minute book can be produced after the certificate is issued.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond to the Registrar's request for clarification within the stated deadline; correct the issue and resubmit without paying a new fee if the original fee was retained.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certificate of Incorporation and Ontario Extra-Provincial Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada (certificate); Ontario Business Registry (extra-provincial licence).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation, the Corporation must register extra-provincially in Ontario through the Ontario Business Registry if it will carry on business or solicit orders in Ontario. Provide a registered office in Ontario and appoint an agent for service. The Ontario registration confirms the extra-provincial legal presence before operational licensing is sought.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Ontario registration is queried or rejected, correct the Ontario Business Registry filing, supply the missing attestations, and resubmit; no substantive re-review of the federal certificate is triggered.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Organizational Board Meeting and Corporate Governance Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors; corporate legal counsel; registered agent for records.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting, adopt by-laws, issue share certificates, appoint officers, establish the fiscal year-end, elect an auditor if required under s.161 CBCA, ratify banking and signing authorities, and set the registered records custodian. Records must be kept at the Ontario registered office as required by s.20 of the CBCA.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: No adverse regulatory step applies to the internal meeting; if a by-law is void for irregularity, pass a curative resolution at the next meeting and record it in the minute book.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Health Canada — Natural and Non-prescription Health Products Directorate (NNHPD); Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery for warehouse/municipal business licensing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Natural Health Product (NHP) Product Licence and NPN Marketing Authorization under the Natural Health Products Regulations, SOR/2003-196; Ontario municipal business licence and warehouse occupier licence.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) and Ontario Ministry of Environment, Conservation and Parks (MECP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full EIA not triggered for pure e-commerce distribution and retail; a Screening-Level Registration may be required only if a physical warehouse operation exceeds provincial waste or wastewater thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC point-source discharges expected. As a cross-border online dietary supplement retailer, any warehouse or fulfilment operation must comply with Ontario Regulation 419/05 for airborne contaminants, municipal sewage and wastewater by-laws for sanitary discharges, and the Environmental Protection Act, R.S.O. 1990, c.E.19 for storage and disposal of expired, returned, or recalled product inventory.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the Ontario Fire Code (O. Reg 213/07), including fire extinguishers, emergency lighting, exit signage, and inspection by the local fire department. Warehouse structural and rack-load inspections are required before occupational occupancy, and the employer must obtain a WSIB clearance certificate for workplace injury insurance and comply with the Occupational Health and Safety Act, R.S.O. 1990, c.O.1, including worker training, hazard disclosure, and right-to-refuse procedures.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC), administering GST/HST under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act and corporate income tax under the Income Tax Act; registration portal is CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) at www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/registering-your-business.html; customs administration through the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) CARM client portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Obtain federal or Ontario articles of incorporation (Corporations Canada or Ontario Business Registry). 2) Request a 9-digit Business Number (BN) via CRA BRO online, by phone (1-800-959-5525), or by mailing Form RC1; the BN carries program accounts RT (GST/HST), RP (corporate income tax), and RC (payroll where applicable). 3) A non-resident corporation without a Canadian permanent establishment uses Form RC4607 (Request for Non-Resident Registration) or, for qualifying e-commerce vendors under the July 1, 2021 simplified GST/HST framework, Form RC4530; supporting evidence includes certified incorporation documents, director identification, and home-jurisdiction registration. 4) Ontario corporate income tax is collected by the CRA on behalf of Ontario under the single-administration agreement, so no separate Ontario Ministry of Finance registration is required for income tax; the Ontario HST component is also collected through the CRA RT account.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. Canadian Business Corporations are taxed as separate legal persons under Part I of the Income Tax Act; Canada has no check-the-box flow-through regime for corporations. A corporation incorporated in Canada is deemed resident (ITA s.250(4)(a)) and taxed on worldwide income, with foreign tax credits available for foreign-source income. Non-resident corporations pay Part I tax only on Canadian-source business income, certain employment income, and taxable capital gains from taxable Canadian property, plus Part XIV branch tax on net Canadian business earnings of a non-resident branch. Territorial scope: full worldwide taxation for resident corporations. No tax-exempt zone or preferential free-zone regime applies in Ontario for e-commerce retail of supplements.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No U.S.-style check-the-box election exists in Canada. Available elections for cross-border corporate structures: (i) ETA s.156 election to treat closely related corporations as a single GST/HST registrant; (ii) ETA s.156.1 joint election for GST/HST filing among related registrants; (iii) ITA s.219 branch-tax treaty election (reduction of Part XIV transmission tax); (iv) ITA s.85 rollover election for tax-deferred transfers of property; (v) ITA s.216/216.1 non-resident elections (rent/royalty and Canadian resource property - generally not applicable to an Ontario-resident supplement retailer). Hybrid mismatch rules (ITA s.18.2 and s.18.3, enacted by Bill C-59, applicable July 1, 2024) operate as mandatory disallowances and deemed-imputation rules and do not offer any elective carve-out.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST - federal Goods and Services Tax plus Ontario provincial Harmonized Sales Tax component, Part IX of the Excise Tax Act, R.S.C., 1985, c. E-15; administered by the CRA.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 (approx. USD 22,000) - small-supplier threshold under ETA s.148. A supplier making taxable supplies in Canada in the course of a commercial activity must register once worldwide taxable consideration exceeds CAD 30,000 in any calendar quarter or over the prior four quarters; non-resident digital and e-commerce sellers must register once Canadian-source remote-supply or fulfillment-warehouse revenues exceed CAD 30,000. Registration is voluntary below the threshold but is generally advisable for exporters seeking input tax credit (ITC) recovery.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance, API-stamping, or digital-invoice validation system. The CRA mandates electronic filing of GST/HST returns for registrants with annual gross revenue above CAD 1.5 million (GST/HST NETFILE), and corporations with gross revenue above CAD 1 million must e-file T2 corporate returns, but invoice data flows have no government pre-authorization or digital stamping. Books and records must be retained for six years (ETA s.286). Any structured e-invoice format (EDI, PEPPOL, PDF/A) is acceptable provided it is legible and supports CRA audit reconstruction.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods: ETA Schedule VI, Part V, s.1 zero-rates a supply of dietary supplements and nutraceuticals at 0% where the supplier (a) ships or delivers the goods to a destination outside Canada, (b) transfers ownership to a non-resident before export, or (c) delivers the goods to a common carrier or shipping agent for export, with export occurring as soon as reasonable in the circumstances (CRA practice: documentary proof of export generally within 60 days). Offshore services: ETA Schedule VI, Part V, s.7 zero-rates services supplied to a non-resident not registered for GST/HST, where the service relates neither to Canadian real property nor to goods located in Canada at the time of supply. Condition: the supplier must retain satisfactory evidence of export (export declaration, bill of lading or courier tracking, customs-broker confirmation, foreign customs entry). Domestic note: sales to Ontario consumers of dietary supplements remain 13% HST taxable, except for natural health products qualifying for the zero-rated categories (vitamins, minerals, and certain herbal remedies with DIN or NPN) introduced by the 2022 Budget Implementation Act and effective October 1, 2025; that domestic relief is separate from and does not alter the export zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA/CARM export declaration (B13A or equivalent eExport and cargo mode reporting) evidencing exit from Canada
Commercial invoice / Canadian customs invoice with HS classification, Incoterms, value, and export destination
Bill of lading (ocean or air), waybill, or courier manifest with external carrier tracking number
Foreign customs entry or delivery confirmation, or carrier certificate proving arrival at destination outside Canada

Payment evidence supporting the cross-border transaction (e.g., bank inward remittance certificate or wire statement; Canada imposes no statutory inward remittance certificate requirement for export zero-rating, but payment evidence substantiates commercial reality)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audit may deny export zero-rating where export evidence is incomplete; the resulting assessment (ETA s.296) claws back uncollected 13% HST with compound prescribed-rate interest from the date the tax would have been remittable. Penalties: (i) ETA s.280 false statements - CAD 250 to CAD 25,000 or 25% of the tax involved; (ii) ETA s.285.1 gross negligence - 50% of the net tax understated; (iii) ETA s.285 evasion - up to 200% of the tax evaded; (iv) prosecution under ETA s.327 and ITA s.239 - fines up to 200% of the evaded amount and imprisonment up to five years; (v) ITA s.163(2) gross-negligence penalty of 50% of understated Part I income. Reassessment windows: four years normally, extended to seven years for negligence or misrepresentation (ITA s.152(4)); refunds and input tax credits associated with false zero-rating are recoverable as debts due to the Crown.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (BOC) as monetary authority and lender of last resort; Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) as prudential regulator of federally chartered banks; Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) as AML/ATF and cross-border electronic-funds-transfer surveillance authority; Payments Canada as operator of the Lynx and ACSS clearing and settlement systems; Department of Finance Canada and Global Affairs Canada as sanction administration authorities. Canada has no foreign-exchange control authority analogous to SAFE; the Exchange Control Act was repealed in 1951, and the capital account is fully liberalized.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full current-account and capital-account convertibility for Canadian-dollar and foreign-currency transactions. There are no exchange-control approvals, no mandatory conversion ratios, and no restrictions on maintaining multi-currency operating accounts (CAD, USD, EUR, GBP) at OSFI-regulated banks. Profit remittance is unrestricted at the banking level but triggers Income Tax Act Part XIII non-resident withholding tax (default 25%; treaty-reduced to 5-15%, e.g., under the Canada-U.S. tax treaty for qualifying dividends, interest and royalties) and related CRS/FATCA reporting. Inbound equity injections require only clear SWIFT purpose coding and FINTRAC EFT reporting for transfers exceeding CAD 10,000; no BOC or OSFI pre-approval is required. De novo establishment of a cross-border e-commerce operation by a WTO-investor parent is generally not subject to Investment Canada Act net-benefit review unless thresholds are triggered or the business is in a culturally sensitive or national-security-sensitive sector.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender obligation and no mandatory conversion ratio or timeline for nutraceutical export receipts; exporters may retain foreign currency indefinitely in OSFI-regulated accounts. The only binding requirements are: (i) FINTRAC large-transaction and EFT reporting for transfers exceeding CAD 10,000; (ii) accurate customs export declarations and controlled-goods classification under the Customs Act and the Export and Import Permits Act, including Health Canada GMP/health-product attestations where applicable; and (iii) inclusion of foreign-source revenue in the Canadian exporter's income tax filings. The statutory timeline for surrender is therefore N/A, and export receivables may be held in original currency under IFRS 9 without any forced conversion date.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium as an ancillary collection and disbursement rail; Low as the primary treasury or capital-escrow provider. Legal constraints: any offshore EMI (EU/UK e-money institution) that directs money-service activity to persons in Canada must register as a foreign money services business (MSB) with FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). Where the Canadian nexus is Ontario, the EMI must also obtain an Ontario MSB licence from the Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario (FSRA) under the Money Service Business Act, 2019. Unlicensed offshore EMIs cannot open CAD clearing accounts, cannot access Payments Canada rails (Lynx/ACSS) without a domestic bank sponsor, and cannot perform Part XIII withholding or maintain a verifiable escrow chain for Canadian corporate capital. Use EMIs (Wise, Convera, Airwallex or similar) only for low-value supplier payouts and card-acquiring settlement; route statutory equity, escrow, tax remittances, and material liquidity through Schedule I banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Hybrid protocol. Canadian-resident directors and signatories may complete remote onboarding using digital identity verification (e.g., Interac Verify, credit-bureau verification, or notarized credentials). Non-resident directors are generally not required to appear physically in Canada if they provide: (i) apostilled corporate documentation (Canada acceded to the Hague Apostille Convention, effective 14 January 2024); (ii) certified passport copies and banker references from a recognized foreign bank; and (iii) participation in a mandatory video KYC/underwriting interview. Because the ISIC 4791 nutraceuticals e-commerce sector is classified as high-risk for AML purposes, all ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) holding 25% or more of the entity must complete a supplemental interview (in-person or by secure video), and the board must pass a treasury-opening resolution designating authorized signatories. In-branch appearance may be required only where the bank's AML risk appetite cannot be satisfied remotely or where beneficial-ownership attestation is incomplete; a full Ontario/corporate registry search and CBCA/OBCA beneficial-ownership declaration will be collected.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ingestible health claims or drug misclassification screening (dietary supplement vs. pharmaceutical)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid Health Canada Natural Product Number (NPN) or Homeopathic Medicine Number (DIN-HM), applicable Site Licence, final label and claims pack, scientific master file, batch-specific Certificate of Analysis (CoA), ISO 22716/GMP certification, product liability insurance certificate of at least CAD 5M, and destination-market import notifications (e.g., US FDA registration or NDI notification, EU/UK novel-food determinations).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border e-commerce chargeback and card-not-present fraud risk causing high-risk merchant classification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 12-24 months of acquiring history, PCI DSS Level 1 attestation, documented refund and cancellation policy, chargeback monitoring and dispute SLA evidence, 3-D Secure adoption, processor underwriting approval, and verifiable customer-verification procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership or multi-jurisdictional supplier structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Consolidated organizational chart identifying all UBOs above 25%, source of wealth and source of funds statements for UBOs, audited financial statements, corporate registry extracts from Corporations Canada and the Ontario Business Registry, and regulated-entity banker references for principal shareholders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear commercial purpose of high-frequency cross-border FX payments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed supplier contracts and pro-forma invoices, OECD-compliant transfer-pricing documentation (master file and local file), shipping and customs entry records, and a written treasury/FX policy confirming no sanctioned counterparties or prohibited transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and export-list screening hits on distribution or fulfillment partners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated sanctions and PEP screening outputs, Global Affairs Canada embargo verification, verified end-user and customer declarations, geolocation-blocking evidence for prohibited destinations, and a documented export-compliance framework.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route via SWIFT MT103 with explicit payment-purpose text, e.g., 'EQUITY CONTRIBUTION - ISSUANCE OF COMMON SHARES' or 'SHAREHOLDER LOAN', referencing the exact Canadian corporate legal name, account number, and corporate registry number for FINTRAC EFT screening. Canada does not use numeric central-bank purpose codes, but clear, human-readable purpose fields are mandatory for OSFI/FINTRAC screening. The injection must be documented by board resolution, share subscription agreements and certificates (where applicable), and an updated Register of Individuals with Significant Control under the CBCA/OBCA; file the annual return with Corporations Canada and the Ontario annual return, complete CRS/FATCA self-certifications (Form W-8BEN-E or W-8IMY for US shareholders), and activate the GST/HST registration number (Ontario 13% HST) for bank onboarding. Inbound equity contributions are non-taxable in Canada; shareholder loans must carry a notional commercial interest rate and contemporaneous loan documentation to avoid deemed dividend or deemed benefit treatment.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rails: (i) SWIFT MT103/MT202 for direct supplier wires with SWIFT gpi tracking; (ii) commercial letters of credit (SWIFT MT700/MT707) for large or first-transaction purchase orders, incorporating Incoterms 2020 and required documents (commercial invoice, packing list, health certificates, Certificate of Analysis, transport documents); (iii) card-network settlement for consumer receivables through high-risk merchant acquirers on Visa/Mastercard, including 3-D Secure and chargeback-monitoring controls; (iv) domestic CAD vendor payments via Payments Canada Lynx for high-value and ACSS for batch payments; and (v) USD disbursements through the bank's US correspondent (CHIPS/Fedwire) to avoid double conversion. Recommended structure: a multi-currency treasury with notional or zero-balance sweeping, a liquidity buffer equal to 30-45 days of payables in each operating currency, automated reconciliation against ERP entries, and monthly FX exposure reporting to the board.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (outrights) up to 24 months
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for matched debt or equity funding
Vanilla FX options, zero-cost collars, and participating forwards
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) solely for restricted emerging-market settlement currencies
Currency options embedded within supplier trade-finance facilities

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery (ServiceOntario)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the anniversary of incorporation each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Corporation placed in default, clearance certificates withheld; five consecutive years of non-filing triggers administrative dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after fiscal year-end; income tax balance due within two months for Canadian-controlled private corporations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month up to 12 months; failure to file permits arbitrary assessment and may impose director liability.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under OBCA, every business corporation must appoint an auditor unless all shareholders waive the appointment annually by written resolution; no revenue or asset threshold applies. Licensing regimes (e.g., Health Canada NHP licence) may contractually require an independent audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; Canadian ASPE for private enterprises; optional IFRS for private enterprises

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: OBCA mandates an Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) register; annual confirmation is submitted through the Ontario Annual Return, and share transfers affecting significant control must be recorded within 15 days. Non-compliance constitutes an offence under OBCA with fines and director liability.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined (15% federal Part I tax + 11.5% Ontario general corporate income tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: For a Canadian-controlled private corporation, the small business deduction reduces federal Part I tax to 9% on up to CAD 500,000 of active business income, and Ontario applies a 3.2% small business rate, producing a combined 12.2% effective rate on eligible active business income. Ontario also provides a 10% manufacturing and processing rate. The federal Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credit offers a 35% refundable credit for qualified Canadian-controlled private corporations.
